predecessors.name: Qarmatians
predecessors.text: Bahrain and al-Hasa, taken from the Qarmatians in 1077-1078

successors.name: Bahrani dynasty of Eastern Arabia
successors.text: Eastern Arabia including the islands of Bahrain, taken in 1253

ledger.x: 1077: Abdullah bin Ali al-Uyuni defeats the Qarmatians and founds the Uyunid emirate.
1119: the Uyunid capital goes back to Qatif.
1253: the Usfurids take Eastern Arabia and end the Uyunid emirate.

wars.name: Uyunid conquest of Bahrain and al-Hasa
wars.outcome: Abdullah bin Ali al-Uyuni, helped by the Seljuk Turks, defeated the Qarmatians in Bahrain and al-Hasa and founded the emirate.

wars.name: Salghurid invasion of Bahrain
wars.outcome: The Salghurid Atabeg of Fars invaded in 1235 and weakened Uyunid power; the page does not say what land changed hands.

wars.name: Usfurid conquest of Eastern Arabia
wars.outcome: The Usfurids, a branch of the Uqaylids and former allies of the Qarmatians and Uyunids, overthrew the Uyunids and took Eastern Arabia in 1253.

certainty.note: The page gives places (Bahrain, al-Hasa, Qatif, Awal, Kuwait) and no boundary; the emirate was a string of oases and ports on the Gulf coast.
